correctness.rationale: For each valid single-wildcard word, the first k wildcard windows expand into exactly 2k deleted de Bruijn edges, and all other windows form a uniquely decodable Euler trail. Degree imbalance forces constant or alternating prefix as appropriate. Directed matrix-tree/BEST gives a first-position count of 2T_n, with T_n=2^(2^(n-1)-n). At the second position, three relevant edge deletions yield a rooted-Laplacian determinant update. The finite shift-register Green-function identity and alternating overlap sums give exact determinant (1-(-1/2)^(n-2))/6, so the two complementary prefixes give T_n(1-(-1/2)^(n-2))/3 completions. Special n=2,3 handled individually. A standalone stdlib verifier independently checks all small partial words, trail counts, integer cofactors and rational overlap identities through n=40; full-length conclusion is the analytical proof, not a finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The source literature gives linear boundary-joker existence but explicitly leaves enumerative questions open generally. The second-position count solves an infinite, natural sharply posed enumeration of all near-boundary partial de Bruijn words: it identifies forced alternating initial structure, a nontrivial rank-three tree correction, an exact parity oscillation, and asymptotic one-sixth loss relative to the first position. The first-position formula is a comparison baseline, not the main research contribution. This is a structural infinite theorem, not a small census or routine numerical increment.
